Validated the production pacing change on `testbed-bjw-can-720dt-1` (Arista-720DT-G48S4, M0) with tagged `SONiC.20260510.17`, build commit `dfb49be0fd`.

Pretest passed: 11 passed, 3 expected skips.

Same-bed A/B/A result for the exact downstream M0 L3 and upstream M0 VLAN policer scenarios:

- **A1, unpatched baseline:** 8 failures / 16 passes. Failures occurred in `checkOriginalFlow()` before mirror/policer validation, including zero-first-packet assertions and partial original-flow receives (`6555`, `7073`, `7437`, `6555`, `8011` of 10,000).
- **B, paced implementation:** 10 sequential iterations passed; **20/20 target cases passed**, zero failures/errors.
- **A2, reverted baseline:** 6 sequential iterations; 3 passed and 3 failed. Failing iterations received `7449`, `8104`, and `7808` original packets.

This same-bed fail/pass/fail control isolates PTF send pacing as the corrective mechanism; the failures occur before DUT policer-rate validation.

Validation interval: 2026-09-23 04:22-09:53 UTC / 14:22-19:53 Sydney. Final DUT health was clean: system state `running`, no failed systemd units, Monit checks healthy, and `gnmi`, `telemetry`, `swss`, and `syncd` running.

Evidence archive SHA-256: `509989693f24a1126301bb20a8015fa103ba0c4b5fc4029f975eb9d894200c92`.

The AST-based unit-test file was removed in commit `dd682b5b7e28097a68367b2166e771e0f7df9abd`; the PR now contains the focused production change only.

**Design review notes / alternatives considered**

- We searched the sonic-mgmt repository for an existing reusable pacing helper. sFlow and VPP/KVM tests contain local count-based batching, while CoPP and DHCP stress tests contain duration/interval loops, but none provides the required fixed-count and duration-based callback semantics with exact accounting and immediate exception propagation.
- We considered extracting shared PTF utilities, but rejected that for this fix because it adds cross-directory import plumbing and unrelated scope. If another caller needs the same abstraction, that can be handled as a separate refactor.
- We considered updating sFlow in this PR, but rejected it as unrelated scope.
- We removed the AST-based unit-test file because it primarily tested source structure and scheduling arithmetic, not the real PTF failure mode. Same-bed A/B/A hardware validation provides the relevant regression evidence.

Reviewed against the base and the KVM tap naming. This is a clean fix and CI backs it (the dualtor KVM Elastictest run passed). The logic is correct and the physical path is preserved.

What I verified
- The KVM-first match is right. On KVM, sonic.xml.j2 names the data-port taps <dut_name>-<n> (ansible/roles/vm_set/templates/sonic.xml.j2:99,111), and self.duthost.hostname == dut_name, so picking the bridge port that startswith "<hostname>-" targets exactly that ToR without the "upper ToR has the smaller vlan suffix" ordering assumption.
- The physical path is not regressed. Physical bridge ports are server-NIC subinterfaces (<port>.<vlan>) that do not start with the DUT hostname, so they fall through the for-else to the original filter-by-"."/sort/zip logic, which is preserved unchanged.
- Fail-loud is preserved: if the bridge has no port for this hostname, the fallback filter yields nothing and it raises ValueError, now with bridge_ports included, which is a nice debugging improvement.

One small, non-blocking note
- startswith("<hostname>-") assumes no DUT hostname is a dash-prefix of another on the same bridge (e.g., "vlab-01" vs "vlab-01-b"). I checked this closely and it is not a real concern today: the baa-* bridge carries exactly one data port per ToR (vm_topology.py create_dualtor_cable attaches only iaa/upper/lower/nic), the mgmt tap <dut_name>-0 is stripped before front-panel mapping (kvm_port.py) so it never lands on the baa bridge, and the real dualtor pairs (vlab-05/06, vlab-11/12, vlab-vpp-03/04, vlab-vpp-05/06, dtor3-dut0/dut1) are never dash-prefixes of each other. If you ever expect a hostname that is a prefix of another, collecting the matches and asserting exactly one (or an exact "<hostname>-<port>" shape check) would make it fail loud instead of silently steering to the sibling ToR. Optional.

Looks good to me. Since this is the enablement helper for the dualtor-aa-vpp cases onboarded in #27663, worth landing them together (or this one first) so the onboarded tests actually pass on the AA VPP testbed.

@augusdn - reviewed head `6fe84f9f9f120f12de41ba23955836270ab844b6`. I recommend addressing these two P2 issues in the opt-in bounded reader before merging.

**Template / DCO / CI:** Required description sections are filled in; DCO, EasyCLA and the applicable CI checks are green. The legacy reader remains the default and is unchanged.

1. **[P2] Stop full-log reads once the boundary is lost.** In [`_appended_lines_command`, lines 232-234](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/6fe84f9f9f120f12de41ba23955836270ab844b6/tests/performance_meter/success_criteria.py#L232-L234), the lost-boundary branch emits the sentinel and then reads both complete log files. The [checker also executes the shell command before checking its permanent `boundary_lost` flag](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/6fe84f9f9f120f12de41ba23955836270ab844b6/tests/performance_meter/success_criteria.py#L273-L282), so every remaining poll repeats those reads even though the sample is already unusable. A reproduction with three polls performed six full-file reads. Please emit only the sentinel in this branch and short-circuit subsequent polls before issuing another DUT command; otherwise this failure path reintroduces the observer load the change is intended to avoid.

2. **[P2] Validate the inode of the file actually read across rotation.** [Lines 225-231](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/6fe84f9f9f120f12de41ba23955836270ab844b6/tests/performance_meter/success_criteria.py#L225-L231) check pathnames with `stat`, then reopen them for `tail`/`cat`. With one prior rotation, a second rotation between checking `syslog.1` and opening it can move the captured inode out of the supported window while the command reads its replacement without emitting the boundary-loss sentinel. A controlled interleaving reproduced a successful 30-second result from the replacement file despite the original boundary being unavailable. Please use verified open file descriptors, or revalidate file identities after reading and discard/retry output if they changed.

The seven committed unit tests passed. Additional checks executed the generated shell commands against real temporary files using Git Bash on Windows; they confirmed normal append/single-rotation behavior and reproduced both cases above. The rotation race was injected deterministically, not observed on a DUT. Please add regression coverage for these two paths.

Bounded mode remains opt-in and is not enabled by the repository today, so I don’t think an immediate revert is necessary. I’ll hold the 202605 backport and prepare a focused follow-up that short-circuits after boundary loss, revalidates file identities after reading, and adds regression coverage for both cases.

## Physical-DUT validation

Validated on the **same physical T2 single-node DUT** (`topo: t2_single_node_max_64p`, single-ASIC) used for the forward-fix, running the real `generate_golden_config_db` Ansible module end-to-end on hardware. Confirms the revert also clears the regression (by removing the `generate_ut2` path that consumed the undefined attribute).

| Case | Module result | `golden_config_db.json` |
|---|---|---|
| OLD 202511 (pre-fix) | `FAILED!` — `AttributeError: … has no attribute 'bgp_confd_asn'` (`generate_ut2_golden_config_db`, line 772) | not written |
| **This revert** | `Success to generate golden_config_db.json` | generated with the ut2/confed path removed (`BGP_DEVICE_GLOBAL` absent) — i.e. the pre-regression behavior |

Raw output (hostnames elided):

```
=== CASE: OLD 202511 (pre-fix) ===
<dut> | FAILED! => AttributeError: 'GenerateGoldenConfigDBModule' object has no attribute 'bgp_confd_asn'

=== CASE: REVERT (this PR) ===
"msg": "Success to generate golden_config_db.json"
BGP_DEVICE_GLOBAL_present=False  CONFED=None
```

Note: this revert restores the pre-#26241 behavior (no UT2 golden_config rendering for `t2_single_node`), so it unblocks deployment but does **not** provide BGP confederation support. If confed support on 202511 is desired, use the full backport #27699 instead.

## Validation: full `bgp/` suite on a physical T2 DUT (revert vs `master`)

This PR reverts #26241 on 202511 to fix the `generate_golden_config_db` `AttributeError` regression tracked in #27582. To confirm the fix is correct **and** introduces no new BGP regressions, I ran the **entire `bgp/` test suite on a physical single‑ASIC VOQ T2 chassis testbed** — once with this revert branch (public 202511 + this PR) and once with public `master` as an apples‑to‑apples control.

### Deploy / config generation
- `deploy-mg` succeeded (`failed=0`); all BGP sessions established (64/64, both address families).
- **0** occurrences of `'GenerateGoldenConfigDBModule' object has no attribute 'bgp_confd_asn'` (the #27582 signature) — the regression is gone.
- `bgp/test_bgp_fact.py::test_bgp_facts` **PASSED** on the DUT.

### Full `bgp/` suite results

| | This PR (revert, 202511) | `master` (control) |
|---|---|---|
| passed | 3 | 20 |
| failed | 3 | 3 |
| errors | 32 | 26 |
| skipped | 134 | 210 |
| golden_config `AttributeError` | **0** | **0** |

(`master` shows more passed/skipped simply because the newer tree carries more `bgp/` cases than 202511.)

### The failures/errors are branch‑independent (testbed infra, not this change)
- **Failed identically on both branches:** `test_bgp_peer_shutdown`, `test_bgp_update_timer_session_down`.
- `master`'s only additional failure — `test_prefix_list_suppress.py::TestAnchorPrefixRegression` — lives in a test file that **does not exist on 202511**, so it cannot be caused by this revert.
- **Errored files are the same set on both branches:** `test_bgp_authentication`, `test_bgp_router_id`, `test_bgp_session_flap`, `test_ipv6_nlri_over_ipv4`, `test_passive_peering`, `test_prefix_list`, `test_seq_idf_isolation`, `test_startup_tsa_tsb_service`. Root causes are testbed‑infra (SSH auth to neighbor VMs and a pre‑existing fixture `UnboundLocalError`) — none touch config generation.

### Conclusion
This revert fixes the deploy‑time regression (0 `AttributeError`s, healthy 64/64 BGP), and **every** failure/error observed on this branch also occurs on `master` → the change introduces no new BGP regressions.

I have changed the approach on this PR, so it no longer depends on an answer about LT2/FT2/UT2.

My original version deleted the confederation override added in 54453e2c4 (#22417). I could not show that was safe for those topologies, only for the one I hit the problem on, so I have replaced it with something that does not require knowing which config field any given topology uses.

It now reads the AS the DUT is actually running BGP in, from `show bgp summary json`, and falls back to `minigraph_bgp_asn` if that cannot be read. Since BGPMonitor is an iBGP session, the running AS is by definition the value it needs:

- non-confederation DUT: running AS is the minigraph AS, so nothing changes
- any confederation DUT: returns the member AS whichever field that topology populates
- unreadable: falls back to the previous default

`get_bgp_confed_asn()` is untouched and keeps its ten other callers.

**Verified on hardware, both approaches giving identical results.** Two physical confederation testbeds, `bgp/test_traffic_shift.py` with `bgp/test_bgpmon.py` as a control:

| | before | delete approach | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BGPMonitor setup errors | 5/5 | 0 | **0** |
| `test_TSB` | error | pass | **pass** |
| `test_bgpmon.py` control | 3 pass | 3 pass | **3 pass** |

I checked each remaining `test_traffic_shift` failure individually rather than assuming - none is the BGPMonitor setup error. They are TSA assertion failures tracked separately, and this PR does not claim to fix them.

The approach also follows what `test_bgpmon.py` already does: it builds its BGPMonitor config without consulting the confederation field, and reads BGP state with `asichost.run_vtysh("-c 'show bgp summary json'")`. This makes the two agree rather than having one file work and the other not.

Good catch @ediwibowo-msft — you're right. The Debian ntpsec package ships with `restrict 127.0.0.1` and `restrict ::1` already in `/etc/ntpsec/ntp.conf`, so setup's `lineinfile` is a no-op there, but the teardown regex removal happily drops those preexisting lines.

Just pushed a follow-up commit that replaces the lineinfile-based teardown with a simple `cp`-to-backup at setup and `mv`-restore at teardown. Same idea for the whole config file (not just the restrict lines), which also lets us drop the pool/tos/server/refclock/interface cleanup regexes since the original file gets restored verbatim.

### Why #25147 does not replace this fix

Both changes relate to background traffic, but they address different layers:

- **#25147 adjusts storm-threshold accounting.** During storm verification, VLAN ports sharing the same `test_neighbor_addr` are grouped into one effective port, with success if any member storms. It does not change traffic generation, PTF interface configuration, or ARP/NDP resolution.
- **#27032 (backport of #24563) changes the actual traffic setup.** For Cisco-8000, it configures a distinct IP on each VLAN-facing PTF interface, updates the corresponding `test_neighbor_addr`, and resolves ARP/NDP for every configured destination. For IPv4, it also sets `arp_ignore=1` and `arp_announce=2` to reduce cross-interface ARP effects from Linux's weak-host behavior.

**The important distinction on dualtor is that unique IPs in the test metadata do not guarantee working per-port forwarding.** The existing dualtor setup already obtains distinct destination addresses from `MUX_CABLE[port]['server_ipv4/6']`, so #25147 normally has no duplicate VLAN-neighbor group to collapse: the denominator and 75% requirement remain unchanged.

However, the old `resolve_arp()` configures/resolves only the first VLAN port and then executes `break`. Other ports therefore depend on pre-existing interface and neighbor state or other fixtures. Starting the background-traffic process alone does not establish that packets reach every intended egress queue.

This PR replaces that first-port-only preparation with explicit per-port setup for Cisco. That can address a failure mode where destinations are already distinct in the metadata, but insufficient ports receive effective background traffic:

```text
Background packets reach the intended egress queue
  + sustained PFC pause on that queue
  -> conditions for PFCWD storm detection
```

In short: **#25147 corrects how eligible ports are counted; #27032 prepares the forwarding paths needed to exercise those ports.** PFC pause-frame injection and effective background data traffic are separate prerequisites; a storm-threshold failure alone does not identify which one is missing.

**Run references and evidence limitation**

- Original run under discussion: https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6aaa5a90cc5c5a13e73d9bc1?testcase=pfcwd%2Ftest_pfcwd_all_port_storm.py&type=console
- Cisco dualtor validation run listed in this PR: https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6aacf26880f8f7db7163b58f

The explanation above is based on the code differences, not a verified log-level comparison of these two runs. ElasticTest authentication blocked raw-log retrieval, so I have not independently confirmed their per-case results, executed sonic-mgmt commits, or port/queue counters. This explains why this change can help where #25147 does not, but does not by itself establish the exact root cause of the original run. Fix inclusion must be checked against the executed **sonic-mgmt commit**, not just the DUT image version.

> Nice root-cause work — I verified the mechanism and it's correct: FRR's "RIB entries" counter (`bgp_table_count`→`route_table_count`) counts radix-tree nodes, not prefixes, so N routes yield ~2N entries, and #22801's drop from `2*NUM_ROUTES` to `1*NUM_ROUTES` let `wait_until` pass at ~50% installation, racing withdrawals against in-flight announcements. Restoring the 2x intent is the right direction, and the withdrawal side (`base_rib` floor, `<= base_rib` assert) is a clean, exact improvement.
> 
> One Major concern before this is solid: the fix hard-codes the **approximate** upper bound (exactly `2*NUM_ROUTES`) as a strict pass/fail floor in both the `wait_until` predicate and the post-loop assert. But "~2N" is not guaranteed — the intermediate splitting-node count depends on prefix distribution (shared internal nodes), and your own evidence shows `6406 prefixes → 12809 entries = 2N − 3`, i.e. _below_ exact 2N. If the 10k injected routes ever produce `< 20000` entries (very possible when the route set shares internal radix nodes), `wait_until` can never satisfy `>= 2N`, burns the full 60s `ROUTE_WAIT_TIMEOUT` every iteration, and the assert then false-fails even though all routes installed. The old code avoided this by using 2N only as a soft `logger.warning`, which this PR removes.
> 
> Suggested safer options (inline): (1) require a margin below 2N, or (2) better — assert on the actual **prefix count** (`show ip bgp` reports "Displayed N routes"), which is exact and distribution-independent, rather than the structural node counter. Could you confirm whether the injected 10k-route set can share internal tree nodes (aggregatable/contiguous block)? If so, the exact-2N floor will flake in the opposite direction on 202605. Non-blocking-if-addressed; flagging as Comment rather than Request Changes since the diagnosis and withdrawal-side fix are right.

Pushed `15489cc9c`. Two substantive changes since the previous revision, plus a note on three things whose real root cause sits outside this repo.

## What changed

**1. The `mpls` FEATURE is now registered as `disabled`, not `enabled`.**

This is the important one. Registering it as `enabled` was verified on a live DUT to break the platform:

```
$ sudo monit summary | grep container_checker
 container_checker    Status failed    Program
$ sudo /usr/bin/container_checker
Expected containers not running: mpls
```

`mpls` is a config flag, not a containerized service — there is no `mpls` docker. With `state: enabled` the image's own monit `container_checker` fails permanently, which fails the **pre-test sanity check for every test on this platform**, not just the MPLS ones. The exemption for the same class of containerless feature (`frr_bmp`) is hardcoded in sonic-buildimage's `/usr/bin/container_checker`, so it can't be worked around from sonic-mgmt.

The conditional_mark gate is `"'mpls' not in feature_status"` — a *key-membership* test — so `disabled` is sufficient to un-skip the tests. Verified: feature still listed by `show feature status`, `container_checker` exits 0, monit reports `container_checker OK`.

**2. `tests/test_pretest.py` and `tests/test_posttest.py` are no longer touched at all.**

Those guards only existed because the feature was enabled. Both loops already skip features whose state isn't `enabled`, so with `disabled` they became dead code. Reverting them removes this PR's footprint on shared, global test files entirely — which also narrows the impacted-area test set.

**3. Skip cleanly when the topology has no T2-facing or no T0-facing interface.**

Gating on topology *type* correctly admits `t1-lag`, but it also admits `t1` variants with no T2 peer. Enumerating all 41 `t1`-type topologies, four have none: `t1-backend` (all `BT0`), `t1-isolated-d128`, `t1-isolated-d32`, `t1-isolated-v6-d128`. Those would have failed with an `IndexError` from `random.choice([])`.

**4. LogAnalyzer ignore for the kernel-MPLS error** — see (a) below.

## Three things whose root cause is upstream of this PR

Flagging these explicitly rather than leaving them to be discovered.

**(a) `intfmgrd` kernel-MPLS error — mitigated here, not fixed.**
Configuring MPLS on an interface makes `intfmgrd` run `sysctl -w net.mpls.conf.<intf>.input=1`, which needs the `mpls_router` kernel module. **No SONiC image loads that module** (nothing in `/etc/modules-load.d/` references it), so the command fails and is logged as an `ERR`:

```
ERR swss#intfmgrd: :- setIntfMpls: Command 'sysctl -w net.mpls.conf.Ethernet76.input=1' failed with rc 1
```

On sonic-vpp this is genuinely benign — MPLS forwarding is done by VPP in userspace via the SAI INSEG entries, so the kernel data path is unused. That's why the ignore is gated on `asic_type == 'vpp'` rather than applied globally: on a platform that *does* rely on the kernel path, this error would be meaningful and shouldn't be masked. The real fix belongs in sonic-buildimage (load the module) or sonic-swss (don't log an ERR where the kernel path isn't used).

**(b) `test_push_label` is skipped, not fixed.**
It injects the push route straight into `ROUTE_TABLE`, and orchagent doesn't install that route into ASIC_DB, so it never reaches the SAI backend. That's a route-management gap in sonic-swss (or an unsupported test method), not something specific to VPP. Pre-existing — it isn't a regression from this change.

**(c) `config interface mpls remove` doesn't restore CONFIG_DB.**
It writes `mpls: disable` rather than deleting the field, so an interface that had no `mpls` key before the test has one after:

```
"Ethernet84":     {"mpls": "disable"}
"PortChannel111": {"mpls": "disable"}
```

`core_dump_and_config_check` notices and auto-runs `restore_config_db_and_config_reload`, so it's non-fatal — the full run below is green. The behaviour is sonic-utilities CLI semantics in pre-existing test code, so I've left it rather than paper over it in the teardown, but I'm happy to add a restore here if reviewers would prefer the test be strictly idempotent on its own.

Pushed `8971943db`. One change since the last revision, plus the local validation results.

## Replaced the LogAnalyzer ignore with a root-cause fix

The previous revision suppressed this error with a LogAnalyzer ignore:

```
ERR swss#intfmgrd: :- setIntfMpls: Command 'sysctl -w net.mpls.conf.Ethernet76.input=1' failed with rc 1
```

That was treating the symptom. The actual cause is that `sysctl -w net.mpls.conf.<intf>.input=1` needs the `mpls_router` kernel module, which **ships in the image but is never loaded** — nothing in `/etc/modules-load.d/` references it, so `/proc/sys/net/mpls` doesn't exist at all:

```
# before
$ ls /proc/sys/net/mpls
ls: cannot access '/proc/sys/net/mpls': No such file or directory

# after modprobe mpls_router
conf  default_ttl  ip_ttl_propagate  platform_labels
$ sysctl -w net.mpls.conf.Ethernet0.input=1
net.mpls.conf.Ethernet0.input = 1        <- the exact command intfmgrd runs, now succeeds
```

So the fixture now loads the module instead of hiding the error. SONiC's own `config interface mpls add` then completes as designed rather than half-failing. This follows sonic-swss's own MPLS test, which does `modprobe mpls_router` in `setup_mpls`, and sonic-mgmt already modprobes in `tests/console/conftest.py` and `tests/test_pktgen.py`.

Verified from a clean baseline (module `rmmod`'ed first, `/proc/sys/net/mpls` confirmed absent), **with no LogAnalyzer ignore in place**:

```
mpls/test_mpls.py  3 passed, 1 skipped
setIntfMpls errors: 0
LogAnalyzer match failures: 0
```

The module is deliberately left loaded on teardown — `modprobe` is idempotent, the module ships in the image, unloading could disrupt anything else using MPLS, and it touches no CONFIG_DB state.

The durable fix still belongs upstream (sonic-buildimage loading the module, or sonic-swss not logging an `ERR` where the kernel MPLS path is unused), but this no longer depends on that.

Reviewed this while investigating a related nightly failure (`lldp/test_lldp_syncd.py::test_lldp_entry_table_after_reboot`). The `/proc/uptime`-based approach is a good direction (monotonic, immune to RTC/NTP drift), but I think there's a correctness issue with the new bound that should be addressed before merging:

**`max_expected_uptime = timeout + wait` is too tight in several existing code paths**, since `reboot()` can legitimately consume more time than `timeout + wait` before reaching this check:
- `safe_reboot=True` path adds `300 + 200 + 20` (docker/db/redis) + `wait + 400` (critical services) + `wait + 300` (interface check) + `wait + 300` (cisco dshell) before this assertion runs.
- `wait_warmboot_finalizer=True` (fast/warm reboot) adds up to `warmboot_finalizer_timeout` (e.g. 180s) before this check, which isn't part of the bound at all. E.g. fast-reboot defaults are `timeout=180, wait=120` → bound = 300s, but `warmboot_finalizer_timeout=180` alone can push real uptime past 300s on a normal, successful run.

Net effect: this risks trading one flakiness source (clock drift) for a new one — false "did not reboot" failures on legitimately-slow-but-successful reboots, particularly in `safe_reboot` / warmboot-finalizer flows. This matches what the automated Copilot review already flagged inline on this PR (line 508) — it doesn't look like it's been addressed yet.

Suggest widening `max_expected_uptime` to account for all the wait budgets already tolerated elsewhere in this function (or basing it on a timestamp captured right before the final check rather than a static sum), before merging.

(Also, minor: using a bare `assert` here instead of `pytest_assert` is inconsistent with the rest of the function and can be optimized away under `python -O` — the Copilot bot flagged this too.)

> @opcoder0 — thanks for building this automation. I found several correctness issues that should be addressed before approval:
> 
> 1. **Migrated-code detection is disabled** (`migration_dashboard.py:1238,1256`). `collect_common2_symbols()` is discarded and `analyze_module()` receives an always-empty lookup, so every symbol has `migrated=False`. Running the current head against the repository produced **263 available modules, 0 migrated modules, and 0 migrated symbols**.
> 2. **Common2 unit-test detection never matches** (`migration_dashboard.py:1228-1236,634`). The generated keys use `tests.common2.*`, but they are compared with source module names under `tests.common.*`. The same run reported zero modules with common2 unit tests, so every module receives the +4 unit-test penalty and the report gives contributors incorrect guidance.
> 3. **Fixture-heavy modules are underscored** (`migration_dashboard.py:518-520,630`). Fixtures are tagged as `kind="fixture"`, but `num_functions` counts only `kind="function"`. The current report omitted 279 fixtures from module size and Project field counts.
> 4. **Existing cards cannot transition to Done** (`upsert_migration_project.py:426-429`). Status is only written when the cached Status is missing, so an existing `Todo`/`In Progress` card remains there even when `migrated=True`.
> 5. **The workflow does not generate the advertised YAML artifact** (`common2-migration-dashboard.yml:69-84`). It omits `--yaml-out`; the successful fork workflow artifact contains only JSON and Markdown, although the README and run summary call YAML the primary artifact.
> 6. **CI is currently blocked by Semgrep**. The four GitHub Actions references need full-SHA pinning. The `urlopen` finding is against a request built from the constant GitHub GraphQL URL and can be explicitly suppressed or refactored after audit.
> 
> Additional gaps: the report advertises tiers 1–6 but emits only 1–5, symbol tiers use module-score thresholds, and `pytest tools/common2_migration/tests` discovers zero tests because the `unit_test_*` files are outside a directory with the matching pytest configuration.
> 
> Please address the data-correctness issues and add focused tests for migration detection, common2 unit-test detection, fixture counting, ranking/tiering, and Status transitions before merge.

As there is no reliable way to detect a code that is migrated unless the contributor updates the information somewhere. If that is really necessary to track, I can consider it at a later date. For now the contributors can open issues for each item and use the issue to track the task to closure.

Update since the points above were addressed — two more commits, both in the "verify correctness, not existence" direction that point 4 was really about.

Auto-generated lossless BUFFER_PG coverage.

The patch deliberately does not carry  BUFFER_PG|<port>|3-4 .  buffermgrd  derives those on link-up from PORT  speed  plus  CABLE_LENGTH , because the profile name is parameterised —  pg_lossless_<speed>_<cable>_profile  — and PFC headroom scales with link speed and cable round-trip time. That is why  BUFFER_QUEUE|<port>|3-4  is pushed while  BUFFER_PG|<port>|3-4  is not: egress profiles are fixed names, the ingress lossless one has to be computed. The platform team confirmed this behaviour, and the NDM production patch we diff against contains no such op.

That left a silent failure mode nothing in the test caught. If the patch omits cable length, neighbour or speed for a port, no lossless PG is ever generated — and the run still passes: apply returns rc=0, the port comes up, BGP establishes, and CONFIG_DB compares equal to the with-T1 baseline. The port simply forwards with no lossless buffers.

Now checked on both sides of the apply:
• before apply — every added front-panel port carries  speed ,  CABLE_LENGTH  and  DEVICE_NEIGHBOR , and the patch pushes no  pg_lossless_*  PG of its own
• after link-up — the profile derived from that port's own speed and cable length exists, is the one the PG references, and is present in CONFIG_DB and APPL_DB both

Deriving the expected name rather than accepting any lossless profile follows what  add_cluster/test_port_speed_change.py  already does; it also catches a port that came up with headroom sized for a different link.

Robustness of the checks themselves.

The CONFIG_DB and APPL_DB readers now live in  util/verify_patch.py  rather than in the DUT-only test module, so the parsing they do is exercised against a stub in the hardware-free suite instead of running for the first time on a device. Hardware-free tests go from 55 to 99.

They handle the shapes a patch and a device can actually present: whole-table, whole-entry and single-field operations, and both forms SONiC writes a profile reference in —  pg_lossless_..._profile  and  [BUFFER_PROFILE|pg_lossless_..._profile] . Profile presence is matched on whole keys rather than suffixes.

Also confirmed the real NDM production patch passes all five preconditions — so the gates are not over-strict and won't fail a valid patch — and that dropping cable length, neighbour or speed, or pushing a lossless PG in either shape, is detected.

One caveat I don't want to overstate: this is all logic-level. The DUT interaction is stub-tested only. The hardware run is pending testbed handover, and I'll report those results here rather than assume them.

Reviewed together with sonic-platform-vpp#262 and sonic-sairedis#1996. The enablement side looks good, and un-skipping `Test_VxLAN_ecmp_random_hash`, `Test_VxLAN_entropy` and `Test_VxLAN_underlay_ecmp` is a real coverage gain for the t1-lag-vpp topology. One scoping suggestion on the tolerance change.

### The statistics check out

I worked through the justification in the `test_vxlan_random_hash` comment independently and it holds up. `packet_count` is per-nexthop (the PTF sender loops over `test_nhs` sending `packet_count` each, and the assertion compares each nexthop against `packet_count`), so with N nexthops the per-bin relative standard deviation really is `sqrt((N-1)/(N*packet_count))`. Reproducing your numbers: N=3, packet_count=1000 gives 2.58% (your ~2.6%), so the 3% default was ~1.16 sigma (your ~1.1); at packet_count=2000 the 7% tolerance is ~3.83 sigma (your ~3.8).

A quick Monte-Carlo over the actual pass condition (test fails if *any* nexthop falls outside the band), assuming idealised per-packet hashing:

| configuration | failure rate |
|---|---|
| packet_count=1000, tolerance=3% | ~46% |
| packet_count=2000, tolerance=7% | ~0.03% |

So this isn't papering over a marginal check — the old parameters were genuinely unusable for any hash that behaves randomly, and 7% still catches a real >7% imbalance. Worth noting this interacts with patch 0016 in #262: at the default VPP multipath tolerance a 3-way group quantizes to 16 buckets (~6% inherent skew), so on VPP the old 3% assertion could not have passed regardless of packet count.

### Suggestion: scope the relaxation to VPP

The tolerance and `packet_count` changes are unconditional, so they also apply to cisco-8000, mellanox, vs and marvell-teralynx. Those platforms have been passing at 3%, which suggests their hashing over the sequentially-incrementing `tcp_dport` distributes more uniformly than the idealised random model — in which case 3% was a meaningful check for them and 7% loosens it for no benefit. Doubling `packet_count` also doubles the runtime of these cases on every platform.

`setUp()` already has a per-asic hook (`data['tolerance']`, set alongside `underlay_tolerance`), so keying the looser tolerance off `asic_type` there — 0.07 for vpp, 0.03 elsewhere — would get the flake fix where it's needed while leaving the other platforms' sensitivity and runtime untouched. Same for the `packet_count` bump if that's easy to thread through.

### Minor

The two Copilot comments above (the `test_vnet_decap.py` skip message and the conditional_mark YAML) both look already addressed in the current diff — the message does mention VPP now, and the vpp skip block is deleted rather than commented out. Probably safe to resolve them.

The failing `impacted-area-kvmtest-t1-lag-vpp` leg is expected until #262 and #1996 land and the submodules advance, as your description notes — flagging only so it isn't mistaken for a real regression at merge time.

> Thanks for the SmartSwitch DPU failure-mode coverage — the scenarios are valuable and the structure is clear. A few correctness/isolation issues should be resolved before merge.
> 
> **1. `prepare_testable_dpus` never restores `dpu_auto_recovery`, and `TestAutoRecoveryDisabled` captures its baseline after the fixture already overwrote it.** `prepare_testable_dpus` unconditionally runs `set_dpu_auto_recovery(duthost, DPU_AUTO_RECOVERY_ENABLE)` on setup (conftest.py ~L75) without first capturing the original value. Teardown only calls `_reset_dpu_recovery_state` (`swss start` + `restart pmon` + wait-ready) — it never restores or deletes the `dpu_auto_recovery` field. Since chassisd treats an absent field as "off", an originally-absent/disabled value is left as `enable` for the rest of the suite.
> 
> Compounding it: `TestAutoRecoveryDisabled.test_no_recovery_when_auto_recovery_disabled` takes `prepare_testable_dpus` as a fixture (which runs first and sets `enable`), then captures `original_state = get_dpu_auto_recovery(duthost)` (~L404) _after_ that override. So its `finally` restore (`if original_state and original_state != DPU_AUTO_RECOVERY_DISABLE: set_dpu_auto_recovery(...)`, ~L443) just re-applies `enable` — a no-op relative to the true pre-fixture state — and is skipped entirely when the original was empty/unset.
> 
> Suggested fix: capture the original value inside `prepare_testable_dpus` before setting ENABLE and restore it exactly on teardown (delete the field via `hdel` if originally absent). Adjust `TestAutoRecoveryDisabled` so its baseline isn't captured after the fixture overwrite, and always restore (including the unset case).
> 
> **2. New CHASSIS_STATE_DB assertions are injected into the shared `pre_test_check` / `post_test_dpu_check` with no capability gating — this can fail existing tests on unsupported images.** The diff adds `assert_dpu_db_state_ready(duthost, dpu_name)` into `pre_test_check` and `assert_dpu_db_state_ready(..., timeout=dpu_online_timeout)` into `post_test_dpu_check` in `common/device_utils_dpu.py`. These are the shared pre/post checks used by existing suites (`test_platform_dpu.py`, `test_reload_dpu.py`, many call sites), not just the new failure-mode tests.
> 
> `assert_dpu_db_state_ready` → `wait_until(..., check_dpu_ready_state, ...)` → `pytest_assert`, and `check_dpu_ready_state` returns `False` when `get_dpu_state_from_chassis_state_db` returns `{}` (no `DPU_STATE|<dpu>` entry). So on any image/platform that doesn't populate the new `CHASSIS_STATE_DB` `DPU_STATE` key/fields (`ready_status`, `recovery_status`, plane states), these common checks will spin to timeout and fail pre-existing tests rather than skip.
> 
> Suggested fix: add a feature/capability check before enforcing the new DB-state assertions (skip rather than fail on unsupported), or scope the new assertions to the tests/images that advertise the DPU state-machine support instead of changing the shared pre/post checks unconditionally.
> 
> **3. `_get_dpu_pcie_bus_info` fallback is dead code and doesn't match its comment.** `_get_pcie_detach_info` already runs `hgetall` on `PCIE_DETACH_INFO|<dpu>` (which includes `bus_info` when present). `_get_dpu_pcie_bus_info` then falls back to `sonic-db-cli STATE_DB hget 'PCIE_DETACH_INFO|<dpu>' 'bus_info'` — the same key and same field. If `bus_info` was absent in the `hgetall` (the only way to reach the fallback), the identical single-field `hget` cannot succeed either, so the fallback is unreachable. The comment says "try platform.json or lspci", but the code does neither.
> 
> Suggested fix: drop the redundant fallback and just `return info.get("bus_info")`, or implement a genuine alternate source (platform.json / lspci) as the comment promises.
> 
> **4. (Grounded nit) Redis-hash line-pair parser drops the final key/value pair on odd line counts.** Both `get_dpu_state_from_chassis_state_db` and `TestPcieFailure._get_pcie_detach_info` use `for i in range(0, len(lines) - 1, 2)`. When `len(lines)` is odd, the last index is skipped and the final field is silently lost. In practice the primary `ast.literal_eval` path handles the normal `{...}` output and this line-pair loop is only a fallback, so severity is low — but the bound is still off. Consider `range(0, len(lines) - (len(lines) % 2), 2)`, or better, use `sonic-db-cli --json` to avoid manual line-pairing (and de-duplicate the two copies into one helper).
>

This defeats the dark-mode protection, including where DPU images are not installed. Cleanup must preserve the original admin state and avoid startup after an untouched/skipped test.

2. **[P1] PCIe test uses the wrong DB contract.** [test_dpu_failure_modes.py:175–195](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/2dd50c76686a177994b29030e39c00cc2c2205c8/tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/test_dpu_failure_modes.py#L175-L195) reads `PCIE_DETACH_INFO|DPU0` and expects `detached`/`reattached`. Consequently, bus discovery skips valid hardware; fixing only the key still leaves impossible state assertions. Discover PCI addresses through the platform API/config and validate actual device/recovery state instead of these nonexistent notifications.

3. **[P2] Setup failures leak enabled auto-recovery.** [conftest.py:102–150](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/2dd50c76686a177994b29030e39c00cc2c2205c8/tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/conftest.py#L102-L150) enables recovery before several fallible checks, but restoration is only after `yield`. If setup raises, pytest never executes that teardown, leaving `dpu_auto_recovery=enable` instead of its original value. Register restoration immediately or wrap the mutations and `yield` in `try/finally`.

CI, DCO and EasyCLA are green, but these test-correctness and isolation issues should be resolved before merge.

@StormLiangMS thanks for the detailed review. Both admin-state preservation gaps are addressed in `559096859` (on top of head `8c9d1cf`), and I also strengthened the disabled-recovery test. Summary below.

**1. Do not power on unconfigured DPUs during teardown** ✅
`ensure_all_dpus_ready` now recovers only DPUs whose CONFIG_DB `admin_status` is explicitly `up`. A missing/empty field (unconfigured DPU) is treated as **not up**, so a skipped or DPU-untouched test can no longer start an unconfigured or intentionally-off DPU. Refactored the CONFIG_DB read into a shared `_get_dpu_admin_status()` helper.
- [`conftest.py` L220-L225](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/5590968596a16a71703ccaee435b6deb237501ac/tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/conftest.py#L220-L225)

**2. Restore the admin state changed by `prepare_testable_dpus`** ✅
The fixture now records each started DPU's original `admin_status` before `startup`, and in the `finally` it shuts back down every DPU it brought up that was not originally admin-up — on **both success and failure**. Recovery-state reset now runs only on the DPUs that remain administratively up (so teardown does not wait on DPUs it just powered off). This makes the fixture self-contained; combined with `ensure_all_dpus_ready` capturing its baseline before setup, a fixture-started DPU is never re-powered afterwards.
- capture: [`conftest.py` L123](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/5590968596a16a71703ccaee435b6deb237501ac/tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/conftest.py#L123)
- restore: [`conftest.py` L167-L187](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/5590968596a16a71703ccaee435b6deb237501ac/tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/conftest.py#L167-L187)

**Non-blocking follow-up — disabled-recovery test** ✅
Added a `get_dpu_reset_count()` helper; the test now also asserts `reset_count` stays constant across the wait (no power-cycle), alongside `ready_status=false`. That is the discriminating signal you called out — a not-ready DPU during chassisd's boot timeout otherwise looks identical.
- [helper](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/5590968596a16a71703ccaee435b6deb237501ac/tests/smartswitch/common/device_utils_dpu.py#L1025), baseline [test L487](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/5590968596a16a71703ccaee435b6deb237501ac/tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/test_dpu_failure_modes.py#L487), assertion [test L505](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/5590968596a16a71703ccaee435b6deb237501ac/tests/smartswitch/platform_tests/test_dpu_failure_modes.py#L505)

Note: I kept the sample window at 90s. Fully proving "no reset throughout the entire configured recovery window" would require waiting past chassisd's default ~600s boot timeout; I'm happy to track that longer-window coverage as a separate item per your suggestion.

Overall this is a meaningful expansion — partial-match and multi-rule tests are logical additions, module-scope VXLAN/VNET setup is a good perf win, and the `_send_and_verify_mac_rewrite` design (build the full expected encap frame, mask only dynamic outer fields, positively verify the inner src MAC regardless of the rewrite path) is a real improvement over master. Not requesting changes — just questions and concerns worth addressing before merge.

### Test-scenario logic looks sound
- `test_single_ip_acl_rule` — /32 match, rewrite path, counter increment. ✔
- `test_range_ip_acl_rule` — /24 match tested with 4 IPs across the range, then rule-modify to a second MAC and re-verify. ✔
- `test_partial_match` — two negative cases: (1) VNI matches, IP doesn't; (2) IP matches, VNI doesn't. Both correctly expect no rewrite + flat counter, since the ACL rule requires both `INNER_SRC_IP` and `TUNNEL_VNI` to match. ✔
- `test_multiple_acl_rules` — two rules, different src IPs, same VNI. Cross-rule isolation is asserted via "the other rule's counter must not move." ✔

### Setup refactor is defensible
- `setup_vnet_ingress_datapath` — repurposing a VLAN-member (server-facing, PTF-connected) port as a routed VNET interface is the right call; without it, ingress traffic never triggers VXLAN encap and the ACL never sees a match.
- Module-scope fixture + `request.addfinalizer` for cleanup is the right pattern — cleanup runs even on partial-setup failure.
- Cisco-8000 `ttl_mode: pipe` for the VXLAN tunnel matches upstream #26084.

### Concerns worth surfacing

**1. Verification claim is empty.** The PR body's "How did you verify/test it?" section is blank. This test only runs on `asic('cisco-8000') + device_type('physical')`, so the green Azure checks are collection/lint only — KVM CI never exercises these tests. Could you paste a run log from an actual Cisco-8000 T0 testbed showing all four tests passing? Given PR #21712 landed with no commits, the bar on this follow-up should be higher, not lower.

**2. Scope mismatch risk — `fixture_setUp(scope="module")` depending on `rand_selected_dut`.** In vanilla pytest, a module-scoped fixture consuming a function-scoped fixture raises `ScopeMismatch` at collection. sonic-mgmt may have `rand_selected_dut` upgraded to module/session scope in some conftest layer — worth a `pytest --collect-only` sanity check against your Cisco-8000 testbed conftest to confirm this doesn't blow up before any test runs.

**3. `backup_config` / `cleanup_test_configuration` operate on `/etc/sonic/config_db.json` without `sudo`.** That path is root-owned on SONiC. If `duthost.shell` isn't auto-sudoing for arbitrary commands, the `cp` silently fails and cleanup can't restore. The current fallback branch does a manual ACL cleanup but does **not** unwind module-level VXLAN/VNET config (Vnet-0, Vnet2-0, Vnet3-0, VXLAN_TUNNEL, INTERFACE rebinding). A subsequent test run then inherits a mutated DUT. Please add explicit `sudo`, and `assert` the backup file exists after `cp` so failure is loud instead of silent.

**4. `test_partial_match` Case 1 packet: `ip_src=202.1.1.200`, `ip_dst=150.0.3.1`.** Ingress interface has `201.0.0.1/24`. On the Cisco-8000 datapath this probably works (loose RPF), but if strict/martian-source filtering is on anywhere in the path the packet gets dropped before VNET routing and the test fails with a datapath-diag dump. Worth confirming in the hardware run.

**5. `create_additional_vnets` runs inside `test_partial_match` and the extra VNETs persist until module teardown.** Not a functional bug — subsequent tests only use primary VNET — but it means test-file selection order via `-k` can leave more residue than expected if module teardown is skipped. Worth a comment in the test acknowledging it.

**6. Temp-file cleanup list is incomplete.** `apply_config_chunk` already removes its own temp files inline, so the explicit list in `cleanup_test_configuration` is misleadingly partial (missing `acl_rule_rule_1`, `vnet_ingress_intf`, `vnet_route`, `acl_rule_rule_vni_match_no_ip`, `acl_rule_rule_ip_match_no_vni`, `acl_rule_rule_multi_1`, `acl_rule_rule_multi_2`). Either drop the explicit list or make it exhaustive.

- `_check_acl_rule_active` assumes `show acl rule` has a `status` column. If a SONiC build regresses this, all rule waits time out with no useful diagnostic — worth a fallback to `redis-cli -n 4 HGETALL ACL_RULE|...` if the CLI parse comes back empty.

The shared priority is deliberate test coverage, not an oversight: the point is to verify that multiple rules at the **same** priority with **disjoint match criteria** coexist and each matches only its own traffic. Differentiating the priorities would remove the very condition under test.

On the "silent reject → false pass" concern — that failure mode is already closed off. `setup_acl_rule()` does not return until the rule is confirmed programmed:

```python
pytest_assert(wait_until(30, 5, 2, _check_acl_rule_active, duthost, ACL_TABLE_NAME, rule_name),
              f"ACL rule {rule_name} not active in STATE_DB after loading")
```

`_check_acl_rule_active` requires `show acl rule <table> <rule>` to report `status == Active`. If a driver silently rejected the second install, the rule would never go Active and **setup would fail loudly before a single packet is sent** — the cross-rule isolation assertion is never reached. So a missing rule surfaces as a setup failure, not a passing test with a flat counter.

---

### 3. `sudo` on `/etc/sonic/config_db.json` — not required, and the backup cannot fail silently

Three independent confirmations:

**a) `duthost.shell` already runs as root.** `AnsibleHostBase.__init__` constructs every DUT host with `become=True`:

```python
self.host = ansible_adhoc(become=True, host_pattern=hostname, *args, **kwargs)[hostname]
```
<sub>`tests/common/devices/base.py`</sub>

and `ansible/ansible.cfg` sets `become_method=sudo` / `become_user='root'`. Adding an explicit `sudo` would be redundant with every other `duthost.shell` call in the repo.

**b) A failed `cp` raises.** `backup_config()` calls `duthost.shell("cp ...")` *without* `module_ignore_errors`, which defaults to `False`, and `base.py` raises `RunAnsibleModuleFail` on non-zero rc. A permission-denied copy aborts the module fixture immediately — it cannot fall through to a no-op cleanup. (Only the `mv` in `cleanup_test_configuration` uses `module_ignore_errors=True`, and that path already checks `rc` and logs/falls back explicitly.)

**c) Empirically confirmed on hardware** in the run above:

```
$ grep -nE "Configuration backup (created|restored) successfully|Backup file not found" logs/test.log
9465:  16/09/2026 20:07:43  test_src_mac_rewrite.backup_config        INFO | Configuration backup created successfully
10904: 16/09/2026 20:14:28  test_src_mac_rewrite.cleanup_test_config  INFO | Configuration backup restored successfully
```

Backup created, backup restored, and no "Backup file not found or move failed" fallback warning.

### Non-blockers

**(1) `fixture_setUp(scope="module")` consuming `rand_selected_dut` — no `ScopeMismatch` possible.**
`rand_selected_dut` is itself module-scoped in `tests/conftest.py`, as are its dependencies `rand_one_dut_hostname` and `duthosts`:

```python
@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def rand_selected_dut(duthosts, rand_one_dut_hostname):
```

So this is module → module, which is legal in vanilla pytest. Confirmed empirically too — the hardware run reports `collected 4 items` with no collection error, which is the `--collect-only` check you asked for.

**(2) `test_partial_match` Case 1 martian source — confirmed on hardware.**
Case 1 (`ip_src=202.1.1.200` on the `201.0.0.1/24` VNET ingress) passed. Note `_send_and_verify_mac_rewrite` does a **positive** `verify_packet_any_port` in both the rewrite and no-rewrite paths — it asserts the encapsulated packet *is* received with the un-rewritten inner src MAC. If the packet had been dropped by a strict/martian-source filter before VNET routing, that verify would have failed and dumped the datapath diagnostics. Passing therefore proves the packet was encapsulated and egressed normally.

**(3) Temp-file list in `cleanup_test_configuration` — the list is correct as written.**
The files you listed as missing (`acl_rule_*`, `vnet_ingress_intf`, `vnet_route`, and the other `_chunk.json` intermediates) are all produced by `apply_config_chunk`, which removes its own file inline:

```python
result = duthost.shell(f"config load -y {file_dest}", module_ignore_errors=True)
duthost.shell(f"rm -f {file_dest}", module_ignore_errors=True)
```

The explicit list exists precisely to cover the two files created **outside** that helper via bare `duthost.copy()`, which are not removed inline:
- `/tmp/acl_rules_del.json` — copied by `remove_acl_rules()`
- `/tmp/inner_src_mac_rewrite_type_acl_type.json` — copied by `setup_acl_table_type()`

The third entry (`vxlan_tunnel_chunk.json`) is redundant with the inline `rm -f` but harmless as a belt-and-braces `rm -f`. Net result: no temp files are left on the DUT.

**(4) Scenario key `multi_vni_test`.**
We use an UNPROVISIONED_VNI along with VXLAN_VNI so the name is still accurate.

Validated this fix against the exact `upgrade_path/test_upgrade_gnoi.py` warm-upgrade failure.

**Nightly reproduction**

- **Plan:** https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6a94295069f529d156ccca77
- **Platform:** Arista-7060CX-32S-C32, T0
- **Image:** `SONiC.20260510.12`
- **Result:** `0 passed`, `1 failed`
- **Failure:** Image transfer and `SetPackage` completed, but the test failed before reboot with `ValueError: gNOI reboot is not supported for reboot type: warm`.

**Validation with this PR applied to the 202605 branch**

- **Plan:** https://elastictest.org/scheduler/testplan/6a94ca2fb7a4f26c75c05a9b
- **Image:** `SONiC.20260510.12`
- **Target result:** `1 passed`, `0 failed`
- **Overall result:** `69 passed`, `8 skipped`, `0 failed`

The validation successfully sent `gnoi.system.System/Reboot` with WARM method `4`, detected `warm-reboot` as the reboot cause, recovered connectivity, and confirmed `SONiC-OS-20260510.12` as the current image. The original exception did not recur.

1. Tautological post-flap convergence assertion (tests/snappi_tests/lacp/files/lacp_helper.py, both `get_lacp_add_remove_link_physically` and `get_lacp_add_remove_link_from_dut`). In both loops the code does:
   ```
   for flow in flows:
       tx_frate.append(flow.frames_tx_rate)
       rx_frate.append(flow.frames_tx_rate)   # <-- should be frames_rx_rate
   assert sum(tx_frate) == sum(rx_frate), ...
   ```
   Since `rx_frate` is populated from `frames_tx_rate`, `sum(tx_frate) == sum(rx_frate)` is trivially true and the post-flap convergence assertion is dead — the test can silently pass while dropping traffic. This is the primary correctness bug; the two logs "Traffic has converged after link flap" and "Traffic has converged after link flap with no loss" are misleading as a result. Fix to `flow.frames_rx_rate`, and prefer comparing per-flow current-iteration values rather than accumulating across iterations.

2. DUT config mutated without any restore/teardown (tests/snappi_tests/lacp/files/lacp_helper.py, `duthost_bgp_config`, and all three run_* entrypoints). The previous `config save` + `cp config_db.json config_db_backup.json` pair was removed; the new path removes interface IPs, creates PortChannel1/PortChannel2, injects `LOOPBACK_INTERFACE` / `BGP_NEIGHBOR` / `DEVICE_NEIGHBOR` / `DEVICE_NEIGHBOR_METADATA`, overwrites `/etc/sonic/config_db.json`, and runs `config reload -f -y`. Neither `run_lacp_add_remove_link_physically`, `run_lacp_add_remove_link_from_dut`, nor `run_lacp_timers_effect` performs any restore, and the tests themselves have no cleanup fixture. The DUT is left permanently reconfigured on both success and failure — this violates hermetic-test discipline and will poison any subsequent test on the same DUT. Add a `try/finally` (or module-scoped fixture with finalizer) that restores the pre-test config (e.g., save the config_db before overwrite and reload it back).

3. Hardcoded testbed-specific `mgmt_addr` written into DUT config (tests/snappi_tests/lacp/files/lacp_helper.py, `duthost_bgp_config`):

   This IP is a specific testbed's address and gets pushed into `DEVICE_NEIGHBOR_METADATA` in `config_db.json` on every DUT regardless of testbed, and (per blocker 2) is not cleaned up afterwards. Derive from `tgen_ports` / inventory / testbed facts, or drop the field.
